t.E586.agn: In its 2014 re-evaluation, EFSA agreed with the earlier SCF opinion that the data were insufficient to set an acceptable daily intake (ADI). For preventing blackspot in shrimps, it found the use toxicologically acceptable as long as residues in the crustacean meat do not exceed 2 mg/kg; it stated that reproductive toxicity data would be needed for any extension of use.
t.E586.body: In two male volunteers, on average 18% of a 1 g dose was excreted in urine in the first 12 hours and 64% in faeces. It has been reported to be excreted in urine mainly in sulphate-conjugated form.
t.E586.found.0: Fresh and frozen shrimps and crustaceans
t.E586.prod: Produced chemically by the catalysed reaction of caproic acid with resorcinol.
t.E586.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no ADI could be set. Acceptable as long as residues in shrimp meat do not exceed 2 mg/kg; additional data needed for extension of use.
t.E586.summary: A synthetic antioxidant. Prevents blackening in shrimps and crustaceans.
t.E586.what: Prevents blackening of the shell in shrimps (melanosis).
